tags.validation_note: Location conflict: thediveglobe.com labels this 'South Coast' but the coordinates (-19.9971) sit at Mauritius' northernmost tip, and tropicalwarehouse.co.uk, dododivers.com and zentacle.com all independently place Whale Rock at Grand Baie / Pointe aux Canonniers on the north coast. Treated as north coast; thediveglobe's label is likely an error or a distinct same-named site elsewhere.

Re-audit 2026-08-13: no local operator or dive database uses the exact name 'Trou aux Biches Reef' for a distinct 12m dive site. The Trou aux Biches area's named reef sites are Anchor Reef (9-19m), The Tube (5-11m), Coral Garden (15-19m), Water Lily Reef, Holt's Rock, Turtle House Reef, 3 Anchors and Lost Anchor (bluewaterdivingcentre.com); the shallow lagoon itself (snorkeling-report.com) is only ~2m deep, well short of the 12m recorded here. Downgraded from validated=true pending a source that ties this exact name/depth to a specific site.

rsis.ramsar.org was unreachable (HTTP 502) on repeated attempts during this re-audit; replaced with advantiko.com and wiotto.com, which independently corroborate the same Ramsar-derived facts (1000-year-old brain coral, ~5m diameter, fish species count). Coral species count conflicts between sources: advantiko.com/Wikipedia-derived aggregate cites 38 species, wiotto.com cites 'more than 50' -- both figures are now noted in the markdown rather than picking one. The '28 genera / 15 families' figure from the prior pass could not be re-confirmed from any reachable source and was removed.

Re-audit 2026-08-13: mauritiusexplored.com (previously listed) does not actually mention Colorado anywhere on its best-diving-spots page and was replaced with divebooker.com, which is the actual source for the '33m average / 40m max' figure already cited in the markdown depth note.

No source uses the name 'Flic en Flac Pass' as a named dive site. Local dive operators list Cathedral, Rempart Serpent, Aquarium, Big Rock, Canyon for this area. This may be a fabricated or conflated site name. Only 1-2 aggregate databases (padi.com region page, scubasnap.app) reference it, not local operators. Re-checked 2026-08-13: additional searches (diveseaurchin.com's full west-coast site list, justdivingmauritius.com, scuba-do.com) still turn up no site by this name; status unchanged.

Re-audit 2026-08-13: lonelyplanet.com URL now returns 404 and diveboard.com returned 503 on repeated attempts, so both were dropped from validation_source (3 remaining, directly reconfirmed). mybasedivingmauritius.com's site-specific listing now confirms 'sharks' (unspecified species) and turtles/trevallies/barracudas at this exact site, so the prior blanket hedge against any shark presence was corrected -- 'grey reef shark' and 'manta ray' remain unconfirmed as species-level claims and are still excluded.

Re-audit 2026-08-13: no Wikipedia article exists for this vessel (minor artificial-reef wreck). Length is unresolved -- directly-fetched sources give no figure at all, while search-indexed (not directly fetchable: 403/503) blogs repeat both ~27m and ~45m; both figures are now presented as an open conflict rather than picking one. Sinking year 2003 confirmed directly via africatouroperators.org. Organizational involvement (Mauritius Marine Conservation Society / Mauritius Scuba Diving Association / Mauritius Oceanographic Institute) could not be confirmed from any directly-fetched source in this pass -- softened to 'commonly cited but not independently verified.' 'Surgeon fish' and 'goatfish' removed from marine life -- not supported by any source found for this specific site; barracuda/tuna/lionfish/butterflyfish remain, confirmed by 2 independent sources (tropicalwarehouse.co.uk, holidify.com).
